claim.rationale: The owner's own head (mine, 0.45) shows much higher usable fraction than cold-exposure sessions (cold, 0.11), likely because the owner can adjust the headband more carefully.
Higher head motion (gyro) should reduce the fraction of usable epochs due to motion artifacts corrupting the signal.
Alpha and theta bands typically co-vary as slow oscillations; positive correlation in log power is expected across sessions.
Beta and gamma bands often increase together during active states; a positive correlation in log power is plausible across sessions.
The activation index (beta+gamma)/(theta+alpha) is higher in mine (0.078) than cold (0.062), suggesting the owner's baseline state is more aroused or the cold dampens high-frequency power.
Mine has lower mean logalpha (0.48) than cold (0.82), possibly because cold exposure increases alpha power (relaxation response) while the owner's baseline is more active.
Longer recording sessions may allow better electrode settling, leading to higher usable fraction over time.
Sleep shows very low alpha (0.17) compared to all sessions (0.73), consistent with alpha suppression during sleep.
Higher head motion should disrupt the activation index by introducing noise that inflates theta/alpha or disrupts beta/gamma balance.
Mine (0.45) has lower usable fraction than mine_sleep (0.96), which is expected since sleep epochs are cleaner and the overnight recording was well-worn.
Beta and alpha are often inversely related (beta up during alertness, alpha up during rest), so a negative correlation is plausible across sessions.
Gamma power is typically low during relaxed states where alpha dominates, suggesting a negative correlation between gamma and alpha across sessions.
